transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood Solutions); Carlos Vega (Meridian Partnerships), Dr. Nina Rao (CTO), Ethan Park (Solutions Architect), Maya Lin (Security)

Summary (auto-gen, brief): Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and Meridian GPU Systems to explore joint go-to-market and technical integration for GPU capacity and co-managed bench offerings. Discussed Meridian's hardware lineup, support for accelerators, target customers (SaaS AI platforms), security/compliance needs, and initial steps for pilot/benchmarks.

Topics: partner model, dedicated capacity, private deployments (VPC/on-prem), security & compliance, benchmarking, go-to-market motions

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on partner motion. Quick intros from our side - Liam is our systems SE, Aisha helps with partner ops.
[00:12] Carlos: Hey Samira, thanks. Carlos here at Meridian, I run partnerships. Nina, Ethan and Maya on the call as well. Appreciate the time.
[00:20] Liam: Hi all. Quick agenda: partner intro, Meridian hardware overview, integration models, security questions, next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Nina: Yep that's perfect. We're especially curious about the Dedicated and Private options you mentioned in the deck we skimmed.
[00:38] Samira: Great. I'll keep the GTM/high level, Liam can go deeper on the infra. But first, can you tell us a bit about Meridian's current focus and customer profile?
[00:47] Carlos: Sure. We sell GPU appliances and cloud-hosted GPU capacity — focus on enterprise/ISVs that need predictable throughput. Our newer product, the Meridian Pod, combines A100-class and custom accelerator boards; we also do colocation and a managed-hosting option. Customers are typically LLM inference SaaS, genomics, and simulation workloads.
[01:10] Ethan: To add, many customers ask for a managed inference layer on top of our infra; that's where we see partnerships with inference platforms like Redwood.
[01:20] Samira: Makes sense. Common partner models we do: capacity supplier (Redwood routes customers to partner capacity or co-managed pools), reseller, or deeper integration where we certify your stack as a verified region in our console. Any preference?
[01:33] Carlos: We're open to all, want to start with capacity supplier + joint pilot. We want to show customers a Redwood + Meridian combo for low-latency inference.
[01:41] Liam: Cool. Technical questions up front: what hypervisor/container infra do you run? Kubernetes, metal, custom?
[01:47] Ethan: Mostly Kubernetes with GPU node pools; a few customers use bare-metal. We use a mix of NVIDIA drivers currently and are testing some newer accelerators from other vendors.
[01:57] Liam: Great — that maps well to Redwood Dedicated, we can run on k8s or bare-metal. Important things to validate: NVidia driver versions, CUDA/cuDNN compatibility, MIG support if you're using A100s, and whether your networking allows VPC peering for Private deployments.
[02:13] Maya: On networking — many of our enterprise customers require VPC peering and strict egress rules, plus KMS integrations for keys. How does Redwood handle KMS and HSM?
[02:23] Samira: We support customer-managed KMS integrations in Private deployments, and have options for HSM-backed key stores for enterprise. We'll share the security whitepaper.
[02:31] Carlos: Awesome. A question on telemetry: our customers want token-level observability for cost breakdowns — is that built in?
[02:39] Aisha: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We can show a demo.
[02:46] Nina: On the subject of latency — do you have benchmarks for cold-start versus warm inference on your runtime? We care about P99 latency for short (8-16 tok) responses.
[02:56] Liam: We optimize for continuous batching and KV cache reuse to avoid cold-start penalties. For typical LLMs with pinned KV cache and warmed workers, P99 for 8-16 tokens is often in the 20-80ms range depending on model and hardware — on A100-level hardware. But we should run a benchmark on your exact hardware to be precise.
[03:18] Ethan: That would be ideal. We'll likely want a standard checklist — batch sizes, seq lengths, quantization, and any kernel tuning.
[03:25] Liam: We'll send a benchmark checklist. It includes model versions, batch distribution, typical prompt lengths, throughput targets, and whether you want quantized models.
[03:33] Carlos: On billing and capacity — how do you do reserved capacity vs burst? If a client wants a dedicated pool but with occasional spikes, can Redwood orchestrate burst capacity?
[03:44] Samira: Yes; Redwood Dedicated supports reserved pools with configurable autoscaling and burst policies into shared capacity or partner pools. Pricing is a mix of reserved commit plus overage/burst rates. We'll include a sample pricing matrix.
[03:55] Maya: Security again, sorry — audit logs and SSO. Our enterprise customers require SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC.
[04:03] Aisha: Redwood supports SAML, OIDC, and RBAC with token scoping. Audit logs are retained per contract; we can discuss retention length.
[04:12] Nina: For on-prem or air-gapped customers, is there an offline installer?
[04:17] Liam: We have a Private deployment option that supports VPC and on-prem installs. For fully air-gapped, we have an appliance/package we can deploy; there are additional compliance steps and support fees.
[04:27] Carlos: On the product side, can the Redwood runtime select kernels for non-NVIDIA accelerators? We're exploring other boards and want to know compatibility.
[04:36] Liam: We have kernel selection logic and we do some non-NVIDIA support, but it depends on which accelerator and the community/runtime support. For custom accelerators, there's usually some engineering to validate kernels. We'll need to know specific board types.
[04:48] Ethan: We'll send a hardware matrix. Quick Q on model hosting: does Redwood host the model binary or do we push images into our infra?
[04:56] Samira: We support both. In Hosted mode Redwood hosts models; in Dedicated/Private we let partners/customers pin binaries or images — we support S3 style pulls and can work with your artifact registries.
[05:08] Carlos: Nice. On compliance, do you have SOC2 & ISO docs we can share with our customers?
[05:13] Samira: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO summaries; we'll send redacted artifacts and a compliance one-pager.
[05:20] Maya: Also need info on data residency and log handling — some customers insist logs can't leave region.
[05:26] Aisha: For Private deployments we can guarantee data stays in customer region. For Hosted deployments we have region controls and retention settings. We'll include specifics in the security pack.
[05:36] Ethan: On the integration path, what does certification look like to be a "verified region" in Redwood? Is it a technical audit?
[05:44] Liam: It's a combination: hardware compatibility tests, throughput/latency benchmarks, security checklist, and basic operational runbooks. Once passed, you show up in our console as a certified capacity option for customers.
[05:57] Carlos: Sounds good. For go-to-market, do you have co-sell motions or marketing assets for partners?
[06:04] Samira: We do partner co-marketing programs, joint case studies, and partner listing in console. We can riff on go-to-market once we have a pilot.
[06:12] Carlos: Great. Two quick pricing questions: margins for resellers and minimum commit for dedicated pools?
[06:19] Samira: Margins vary by contract; for Dedicated we usually look at 3-6 month soft commits for pilots and a larger 12-month commit for production. We'll share a sample contract skeleton.
[06:30] Maya: Security follow-ups: do you support customer-managed encryption keys for model artifacts? Some customers require that.
[06:36] Liam: Yes, customer-managed keys are supported for Private and Dedicated with the right integrations. Hosted has options but with more constraints.
[06:44] Ethan: Back to performance — do you have experience with KV cache warmup across GPU types? We have a mixed fleet so cache portability is a concern.
[06:52] Liam: We manage KV cache and there are compatibility considerations if you mix quantization levels or kernel optimizations. It's ideal to standardize a few image types per fleet; we'll note that in the checklist.
[07:04] Carlos: Any red flags we should know before committing to a pilot together?
[07:08] Samira: Nothing major; main things are driver compatibility, networking (VPC peering and firewall rules), and agreeing on pilot success metrics (latency, throughput, cost targets). If we align on those, pilots are straightforward.
[07:22] Nina: Let's talk about success metrics — for us, a pilot that demonstrates P99 < 120ms for 16-tok completions at 200 RPS would be interesting. Does that sound achievable?
[07:31] Liam: On A100 or comparable, that seems achievable with proper batching and warmed workers. We'll validate in benchmark.
[07:38] Ethan: We'll prepare sample workloads and expected distributions.
[07:42] Samira: Perfect. We'll also want a short integration doc for your ops team.
[07:47] Carlos: On legal side, any NDA or partner agreement templates?
[07:51] Samira: Yes we have a partner agreement and NDA; I'll drop the standard templates.
[07:56] Maya: A few more security items: penetration testing cadence, SSO provisioning, and whether you support per-tenant encryption keys.
[08:05] Liam: We support pen test reports shared under NDA, SAML/SCIM provisioning, and per-tenant keying for certain tiers. We'll include those details.
[08:15] Aisha: Quick note — we have a partner enablement kit that covers tech integration, how adding a verified region shows up in console, and co-marketing assets. We'll send that after the call.
[08:26] Carlos: Nice. On timeline: if we start a pilot, how long to get a certification path done? 3-6 weeks?
[08:33] Liam: For a basic pilot and perf validation, typically 3-4 weeks if both sides are responsive. Full certification with security audit could be 6-8 weeks.
[08:43] Ethan: That timeline aligns with our internal roadmaps.
[08:47] Samira: Great. I'll recap next steps at the end. Any final questions before we move to a few technical details, Liam?
[08:53] Carlos: No, sounds good.
[08:55] Liam: Quick technical detail — do you expose metrics through Prometheus endpoints?
[08:59] Ethan: Yes, metrics are exposed and we can set up a Prometheus scrape or send to your telemetry collector.
[09:06] Liam: Perfect, that helps for SLO tracking. Also, do you have a preferred artifact registry for model binaries?
[09:12] Carlos: We typically use an S3-backed artifact store and sometimes Artifactory.
[09:17] Samira: That works. We'll note artifact pull methods in the integration doc.
[09:22] Nina: Another ops question — do you support GPU multiplexing for lower-cost inference (multi-tenant) or is it mostly single-tenant for predictability?
[09:32] Liam: Redwood can run multi-tenant or single-tenant depending on policy. For strict enterprise SLAs we often do single-tenant pinned workers. For cost-sensitive workloads we enable multi-tenant with isolation controls.
[09:45] Carlos: Great. Is there any existing Meridian customer you'd want us to introduce to Redwood for pilot?
[09:51] Carlos: We have a SaaS company running LLM chat for support use cases that might be a good pilot candidate. We'll propose internally.
[09:58] Samira: Excellent. That could accelerate GTM.
[10:02] Aisha: On contractual logistics, we typically start partner pilots under a pilot SOW. We'll share a template.
[10:10] Carlos: Ok, switching gears — are there any special requirements to onboard a new partner region in your console (IP allowlists, certs)?
[10:18] Liam: We do require control plane connectivity, cert exchange, and a small tunnel or VPC peering for control-plane telemetry. We'll provide a checklist.
[10:26] Maya: One more question on logs — can customers opt to have logs forwarded to their SIEM instead of Redwood storing them?
[10:32] Aisha: Yes, log forwarding to customer SIEM is supported for Dedicated/Private. We can configure retention and forwarding rules.
[10:40] Samira: Okay I'm gonna do a short recap of next steps and owners.
[10:44] Samira: Action items: Samira sends deck and sample pricing (due 3/5); Liam sends benchmark checklist and perf questions (due 3/6); Maya to share compliance questionnaire (due 3/9); Redwood to send security whitepaper and partner enablement kit (3/6). We'll also set a follow-up technical deep dive for week of 3/16. Does that capture it?
[11:05] Carlos: Yes that looks right. Thanks.
[11:08] Nina: Quick note — for benchmark, we'll want to include quantized model runs as well as FP16 baseline.
[11:14] Liam: Noted, we'll include quantization permutations.
[11:18] Ethan: We'll prepare the hardware matrix and sample workloads and send by Friday.
[11:22] Samira: Perfect. Any objections or deal-breakers we haven't covered?
[11:27] Carlos: None from us.
[11:29] Maya: All good.
[11:31] Samira: Thanks again everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite for the tech deep dive.
[11:37] Carlos: Appreciate it. Bye.

(Recording ends)
